question.problem:
The matrix $Q$ is given below. Let ${q}_{1}$, ${q}_{2}$,  ${q}_{3}$, and ${q}_{4}$ be the respective columns of $Q.$ Determine if $B=\text{{}{q}_{1},{q}_{2}\text{}}$ is a basis of $\text{Col}(Q).$ If that is the case, find ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}$, where ${q}_{4}={x}_{1}{q}_{1}+{x}_{2}{q}_{2}.$

$$
Q=[\begin{aligned}4 & 1 & -2 & 4 \\ 0 & 4 & 2 & 4 \\ 0 & 2 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$
question.worked_solution:
First, we reduce the matrix $Q$ to reduced row echelon form (RREF):

$$
\begin{aligned}Q & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 1 & -2 & 4 \\ 0 & 4 & 2 & 4 \\ 0 & 2 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{4}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}4 & 1 & -2 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & \frac{1}{2} & 1 \\ 0 & 2 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-2){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}4 & 1 & -2 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & \frac{1}{2} & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-1){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 & -\frac{5}{2} & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & \frac{1}{2} & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{4}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -\frac{5}{8} & \frac{3}{4} \\ 0 & 1 & \frac{1}{2} & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

From the matrix above, we see that the pivot columns are the $1$st and $2$nd columns. So, a basis of $\text{Col}(Q)$ is $\{{q}_{1},{q}_{2}\},$ that is to say,

$$
B=\{[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\}.
$$

Now, since the $4$th column of the reduced matrix is a non-pivot column, then the entries in that column tell us the coefficients needed to express ${q}_{4}$ as a linear combination of all the other columns in the original matrix. So, we have

$$
{{[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 4 \\ 2\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{q}_{4}}={{(\frac{3}{4})}_{⏟}}_{{x}_{1}}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{q}_{1}}+{{(1)}_{⏟}}_{{x}_{2}}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4 \\ 2\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{q}_{2}}.
$$

This gives us ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}=\frac{3}{4}\cdot 1=\frac{3}{4}.$
